condition-all-voted-for.how: `vote::for_permanents(g, source, you, &candidates)?` returns the tally as a `Vec<u32>` and `vote::most_votes` the winners, in the effect's own locals, which is all 'kept for later instructions' needs: an effect reruns deterministically after each answer, so a local holds for the whole resolution. For word options: `let mut war = 0; for p in g.state().turn_order_from(you).collect::<Vec<_>>() { if players::reached(g, p) { if choose::one_of(g, p, source, labels.clone())? == 0 { war += 1 } } }`. `Condition VotedFor` is then `if picks[i] == 0`.

condition-as-cast.how: optional_cost: Some(OptionalCost::new(Cost{behold: Some((1, dragon_card_in_hand, ..)), ..})): a filter testing q.obj(id).zone.is(ZoneKind::Hand) turns behold into 'reveal a Dragon card from your hand', since behold_candidates retains by filter. Dragon's Fire: the same filter without the hand test. 'If you revealed': item.paid; an entering creature reads it from q.state().left_stack(id). 'Or controlled a Dragon as you cast': cast_fact, history.fact_as_cast.
condition-as-cast.partial: No hand-written card uses behold as a hand-only reveal; a behold-reading card ('whenever you behold') would see it.

condition-chose-nth.how: Took or did within one effect: a local (Tempt with *, Eureka, Hypergenesis). Turn records: q.history() over casts, Event::DieRolled, Activated events (Eelectrocute, Elvish Refueler, Laboratory Drudge, Spider-Man 2099, Izzet Generatorium). Value chosen: chosen_* .
condition-chose-nth.partial: Reading a bare event type past the History helpers is unverified. Saga "was monarch at turn begin" needs a scan from TurnBegan.

condition-graveyard-position.how: The held code read cards[..at] as above, but a graveyard's top is its last: above is cards[at + 1..]. The data says 'above' of what the card says 'directly above', so the line is read for it. Ashen Ghoul stays a hole: 'above this card' names no graveyard, so Cantrip's graveyard_order_matches_oracle test refuses reads_graveyard_order and the order would never be asked.
condition-graveyard-position.note: Marked as a misread: the field exists for exactly this.

condition-had-extreme.how: Compare locals from a loop of choices.

condition-most-votes.how: `vote::for_permanents(g, source, you, &candidates)?` returns the tally as a `Vec<u32>` and `vote::most_votes` the winners, in the effect's own locals, which is all 'kept for later instructions' needs: an effect reruns deterministically after each answer, so a local holds for the whole resolution. For word options: `let mut war = 0; for p in g.state().turn_order_from(you).collect::<Vec<_>>() { if players::reached(g, p) { if choose::one_of(g, p, source, labels.clone())? == 0 { war += 1 } } }`. `Condition VotedFor` is then `if picks[i] == 0`.
condition-most-votes.note: `vote` has no options form yet: one shared function (`for_options`) would cover 27+15 cards. That is cantrip-mechanics, no core change.

condition-searched.how: The search the condition reads is itself held ('operation Search', 'search with several find clauses'). search_zone_and_or_library searches one other zone along with the library, while these cards search two (graveyard and hand).
condition-searched.partial: Takes one zone; three-zone cards combine calls.

condition-subset-meets.how: Each is a plain fn: `fn all_share_a_color(q) -> bool` (an `and` of `ColorSet`s over `q.state().battlefield()`); Dead Ringers: `chars(a).colors == chars(b).colors`; subset-sums walked by plain iteration.
condition-subset-meets.note: A target restriction across several slots needs a slot filter reading earlier chosen targets from `Asker`; not checked in every card.

condition-targets-match.partial: The read of targets exists (stack item), but both cards use it for flash, and flash_if is judged "only as the casting begins", before targets are chosen. Timely Ward also needs commander.

counter-kind-acorn.how: None today: `add_counters`, `Entering.counters`, `remove_counters` and `Cost` all take a `CounterKind`, so a card cannot name a kind the enum lacks. Once listed, a card spells it as hand-written Wishclaw Talisman does: `entering.counters[CounterKind::Wish as usize] += 3`, `remove_counters(CounterKind::Wish, 1)` in a cost, `g.add_counters(id, CounterKind::Wish, 1)` in an effect.
counter-kind-acorn.note: Mechanical, not a design gap: one line each in `counter_kinds!` (index, variant, name), all 173 in one commit; commit 351845f4e added Bounty with one line in vocab.rs. CounterKind::ALL drives proliferate, 'remove all counters', host views and the client, and dotnet/src/Cantrip.Core/CounterNames.cs s
counter-kind-acorn.partial: None for those that exist once added. A card that writes a look-alike kind (Charge for a storage counter) plays differently under proliferate, Vampire Hexmage-style removal, 'storage counter' readers and the client's pill, so that is not a form.

counter-kind-ember.note: Mechanical, not a design gap: one line each in `counter_kinds!` (index, variant, name), all 173 in one commit; commit 351845f4e added Bounty with one line in vocab.rs. CounterKind::ALL drives proliferate, 'remove all counters', host views and the client, and dotnet/src/Cantrip.Core/CounterNames.cs s
counter-kind-ember.partial: None for those that exist once added. A card that writes a look-alike kind (Charge for a storage counter) plays differently under proliferate, Vampire Hexmage-style removal, 'storage counter' readers and the client's pill, so that is not a form.

counter-kind-rad.note: `PlayerCounter` has Poison, Energy, Experience. Rad needs a Player field, a Game verb, the precombat-main trigger (mill N, lose life per nonland, remove that many) and 'if a player has rad'. The tracker's `rad-counters` row, in another partition, is the real one: 20+ cards.

counter-kind-rally.how: None today: `add_counters`, `Entering.counters`, `remove_counters` and `Cost` all take a `CounterKind`, so a card cannot name a kind the enum lacks. Once listed, a card spells it as hand-written Wishclaw Talisman does: `entering.counters[CounterKind::Wish as usize] += 3`, `remove_counters(CounterKind::Wish, 1)` in a cost, `g.add_counters(id, CounterKind::Wish, 1)` in an effect.
counter-kind-rally.note: Mechanical, not a design gap: one line each in `counter_kinds!` (index, variant, name), all 173 in one commit; commit 351845f4e added Bounty with one line in vocab.rs. CounterKind::ALL drives proliferate, 'remove all counters', host views and the client, and dotnet/src/Cantrip.Core/CounterNames.cs s

counters-a-player-has-by-kind.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: The player state readers and give calls.

counters-of-a-kind-chosen-as-the-effect-.how: remove_counters_up_to is 'any number' only. 'Remove X counters' is mandatory: choose_counter_kind and remove_counters once per counter.

counters-put-as-a-cost-on-another-object.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: Thought Gorger: put counters and discard in the effect; The Serpent Society precedent.
counters-put-as-a-cost-on-another-object.partial: Thought Gorger needs no cost at all: it's an effect.

counters-the-event-put.how: Not landed. g.counters_put_by in the held code doesn't exist. Event::CountersPut carries one kind per event, so 'those counters' across kinds needs a read of the batch.

craft-materials-that-must-have-something.how: `craft::materials` checks each card on its own; a filter for two that share a type is pairwise.
craft-materials-that-must-have-something.note: Need to read how `Materials` selects, and whether the choice can be validated together.

cumulative-upkeep-paid-other-than-in-man.how: The card's own Effect at upkeep: add the age counter, then loop or g.may_pay(Cost::..) for each age: hybrid symbols one payment each; draw, flip, discard, control as plain calls: cumulative_upkeep::ability(pay, text) takes an Effect.
cumulative-upkeep-paid-other-than-in-man.note: Check against row 87 for the paid events.
cumulative-upkeep-paid-other-than-in-man.partial: Several separate may_pay questions instead of one payment: partial payment is impossible by CR 118.8; refund not possible.

damage-prevented-by-an-effect-of-this-ab.how: Prevented::total is told to then, and nothing stores it for a later delayed ability.
damage-prevented-by-an-effect-of-this-ab.note: PreventionDef has no then, so nothing reports the amount to a delayed ability; see feature 1.

damage-source-kind-spell.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: `q.history().damage_dealt().any(|d| d.source == spell)`: object rows are never deleted, so the id still answers.

damage-to-each-permanent-a-card-type-los.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said:

delayed-ability-about-objects-and-a-play.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: entered_with link and Fired.data.

delayed-trigger-at-main-phase-begins.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: delayed::at_your_next_main_phase(g, item, 0, subject), DelayedWhen::Step or UntilNextTurnOf.
delayed-trigger-at-main-phase-begins.partial: A stated other player's next turn takes a matcher.

delayed-trigger-starting-players-next-tu.how: DelayedWhen::Step { on_turn_of } fires this turn when made on your own turn before that step; 'your next turn' is not that. at_your_next_main_phase is only for main phases. ExtraTurnStep needs a known turn number, which extra turns make unknown.
delayed-trigger-starting-players-next-tu.partial: A stated other player's next turn takes a matcher.

delayed-trigger-this-turn-with-no-end-in.how: Landed. The data's event is WhenPlayerCastsTheirNextSpellOrActivatesTheirNextAbilityThisTurn: `future_expiry` now gives it EndOfTurn, so it is DelayedWhen::NextThisTurn (Magus Lucea Kane, Repeated Reverberation). Seraph was a false hole: its 'this turn' is the trigger's own, so the check now asks for 'next ... this turn' in one sentence, and Seraph holds on trigger-event-player-loses-control.

destroyed-together-some-that-can-t-be-re.how: `destroy_all` and `destroy_all_no_regen` are each one batch: lands chosen, the land creatures can't be regenerated and the rest can, destroyed at once. Needs one destroy with a per-object no-regeneration set.

duration-during-controllers-next-untap-s.how: g.exert is right for a named closed set and landed there. The rest are open sets. A resolving 'doesn't untap' that changes no characteristics or controller modifies rules, CR 611.2c. No EffectKind says it. Keyword::DoesNotUntap is the permanent's own: granting it would end under Humility and count for Muraganda Petroglyphs (card.rs documents UntapBan as never a keyword). EffectKind::CantBecomeUntapped is stronger, it also stops effects that untap and keeps stun counters. untap_bans sit on a battlefield source with its abilities, so a source losing them would end a resolved effect. Needs an EffectKind in Cantrip.
duration-during-controllers-next-untap-s.note: The Duration enum is the wrong place to look: the mechanic is a mark, exerted_by. No hand-written card uses it for this wording yet.
duration-during-controllers-next-untap-s.partial: No event is raised, so 'whenever you exert' does not trigger (right: these cards do not exert). It marks the permanents chosen at resolution only; a text that covers permanents arriving later (CR 611.2c open set) is not covered, nor one with its own controller-relative twist.

duration-during-controllers-next-untap-s.partial: The second skip is put on by a visible delayed trigger instead of a rule; it can be responded to.

A resolving 'doesn't untap' that changes no characteristics or controller modifies rules, CR 611.2c. No EffectKind says it. Keyword::DoesNotUntap is the permanent's own: granting it would end under Humility and count for Muraganda Petroglyphs (card.rs documents UntapBan as never a keyword). EffectKind::CantBecomeUntapped is stronger, it also stops effects that untap and keeps stun counters. untap_bans sit on a battlefield source with its abilities, so a source losing them would end a resolved effect. Needs an EffectKind in Cantrip.

instruction-choose-one.how: Landed where the words are the card's (Abundance's Land/Nonland, the destination labels). Trait Doctoring and Whim of Volrath are data bugs: the color option comes back with Duration::Indefinite where Oracle ends both at end of turn, and printed_options holds them for that. Cloak and Dagger, Entwined: the source drops 'until they leave the battlefield' (printed_options holds any choice that says so). Bison Whistle: the source makes 'Otherwise' a free fourth option, so a Bison could go to a graveyard; Oracle doesn't allow it.
instruction-choose-one.note: Tracker row says so itself: the AST carries no labels. A generator gap, not an API gap.
instruction-choose-one.partial: Cantrip needs nothing; the generator must lift the two option labels from card text. "Choose a card from your hand or graveyard" (Agonizing Remorse, Covetous Urge) is a ChooseCards over two zones, not a labelled choice. Villainous lines are row villainous-choice.

keyword-action-reroll-stored-dice.how: `let rolls: Vec<Roll> = (0..n).map(|_| g.roll_die(you, 6)).collect();` then read `r.result` in locals: keep highest with `.max()`, two in order with a `choose::one_of` over the two results.

keyword-action-reroll-stored-dice.partial: Each die is its own `Event::DieRolled`, so 'whenever you roll one or more dice' fires per die unless batched (`once_per_batch`), and 'store those results on it'/'reroll stored' (Centaur of Attention) need the stored values on the object: use `Done`-style notes or counters, an Unfinity case.

object-filter-could-produce.how: The audit is wrong. `adds` misses abilities whose mana comes from their own effect, and it misses replacement effects (CR 106.7). producible_types is pub(crate), so no card can read what a land could produce (Break the Ice, Obsidian Charmaw).

object-filter-damaged-by.how: Lands for an instant or sorcery whose only ability is the spell and which has one damage instruction: what its object dealt damage to is what it dealt damage to that way (Ghired's Belligerence, and Aurelia's Fury's creatures). Huatli and Demonfire stay held: an ability's source can deal other damage, and Demonfire's Hellbent is another ability.
object-filter-damaged-by.note: A clear misread: the proposed name is the real one. Four written cards use it.
object-filter-damaged-by.partial: Players dealt damage this way (Aurelia's Fury) are not permanents: walk `g.history().damage_dealt()` for `Target::Player`.

object-filter-dealt-excess-by.how: `if let Some(r) = g.damage_result(src, t, n) { if r.excess > 0 { hit.push(t) } }` in a loop, or `Event::Damage.recipient_excess` from the history.

object-filter-has-activated-ability.partial: Cards in a library or graveyard read their printed abilities. Abandoned Sarcophagus still needs a cast-from-graveyard grant (`granted_ways`), which exists.

Cascade, Fading, Modular, Unearth, Level up and Cumulative upkeep are identified only by a const or fn, and Disturb, Awaken, Partner, Doctor's companion, Rampage, Soulbond, Blitz, Embalm and Eternalize have no engine field. Without matching ability text, those stay holes. Flashback also needs harmonize and beam me up excluded and grants read (permissions, GrantedWay).
object-filter-has-keyword-family.note: The tracker's `q.has_keyword_ability` would be a convenience, not a capability. Rows with Soulbond, Blitz, Disturb, Rampage etc. need those mechanics first; the query itself is free once the ability's text exists.
object-filter-has-keyword-family.partial: A granted way a permanent gives (Iroh's `GrantedWay { flashback: true }`, escape, mayhem) is on the giver, not the card, so 'has flashback' for a granted one means walking `q.permanents_of(p)` and calling their `granted_ways`. object-filter-noted.how: `entering.chosen_subtype` kept as `Choices`; Saga chapters: a word per chapter from `note_done`. Reading: `q.obj(me).choices`.
object-filter-noted.partial: Favored Enemy (as it enters) is fine; Long List notes several and a chapter's note needs a word, which `Done` doesn't carry: a marker effect per word. Has its own digital part.

object-filter-nth-cast.partial: The spell doesn't literally have cascade. Rain of Riches reads treasure mana: row 109.

object-filter-nth-chosen.partial: Illusionary Terrain keeps two land types: see a-land-type-chosen-second.

object-filter-on-stack.how: `q.state().stack.iter().filter(|i| i.ability.is_some())`: a `StackItem` knows its `source`, its `ability`; a filter over items is one line. `targets::activated_or_triggered_ability_*` are existing filters.
object-filter-on-stack.note: 'An ability shares its object with its source' is false: the item carries the ability ref.

object-filter-paired-with.how: Keep the pair as continuous effects, which the state already relates: `g.add_effect(a, b, EffectKind::AddAbility(AbilityRef::delayed(card, 0)), Duration::AsLongAs(card, 0))` and the mirror, the `lasting[0]` condition being 'you control both'. `paired_with(q, id)` reads `q.state().effects.iter().find(|e| e.source == id && matches!(e.kind, EffectKind::AddAbility(_)))`. The soulbond trigger is `THIS_ENTERS` or `when(ZONE_CHANGE, another creature you control enters)`, offered only while both are unpaired.

object-filter-shares-color-with-mana.note: C.A.M.P.: fortify and tapped-for-mana stack trigger: row 21.

object-filter-targetable-by.how: The audit is wrong. 'Could target' needs the slot's filter under the rules' Given (its X, its subject, the slot's player). The plain Query has announced_x None, and the modal and kicker specs are private (target_specs). Beamsplitter Mage, Exterminator Magmarch and Feather stay held.

object-filter-was-attached-to.how: Non-Aura lines land, read through the Unattached records. Hateful Eidolon is a data bug: the AST counts Auras on the battlefield, but state-based actions have already put them in graveyards. Held because its line says 'Aura'.

object-reference-affected.how: The function's own arguments: CostChange takes (q, source, player, costed, targets).
object-reference-affected.note: A misread: functions are told their object.
object-reference-affected.partial: Space Beleren and perpetual cards not.

object-reference-bound.how: A walk is a `for` loop: the object is its loop variable. Mind Grind: `for p in opponents { let mut lands = 0; .. reveal until ..}`.
object-reference-bound.note: Forms a problem of the generator's AST, not Cantrip's.

object-reference-earlier.how: Dack Fayden, Helping Hand: the AST lost 'choose a different opponent', so each pick shuts out the rest, which a walk of independent picks doesn't do. Held because its line says 'a different'.

object-reference-granter.how: The card lookup the audit gives is ambiguous with two copies, but needs no fallback: a static grant's stamp is its source's timestamp (layers.rs GEntry), and a resolved grant's is the effect's, so item.acquired names the giver exactly.
object-reference-granter.note: `ActionOption::granted_by` is what the core already uses for the sacrifice, so the fact exists; only triggered abilities lack a direct read.
object-reference-granter.partial: The card-based lookup is ambiguous when two copies of the Aura sit on one creature: then the effect's `Acquired.stamp` against `state.effects` picks the right one. An ability still on the stack after the granter left needs last-known handling; a text-changed or copied granter likewise.

object-reference-haunted-by.how: The relation is a link: `g.link_exiled(me_in_exile, Linked::..)` is one form, but the plain form is a trigger that functions in exile. When the haunt card dies (or a haunt spell resolves): `g.exile_with(&[me], ..)` naming the haunted creature, recording with `g.note_done`. The 'haunted creature dies' ability is `when(ZONE_CHANGE, ..).functions_in(ZoneKinds::EXILE)` matching the haunted object from the note, and a filter reads it the same way.

object-reference-made-here.how: `q.obj(me).entered_with`, the ability's link to what the source put in: `Necromancy`'s read of `entered_with` is this; or the `reflexive`/`delayed_trigger_about` holding the object id.

object-reference-paired-with.how: Keep the pair as continuous effects, which the state already relates: `g.add_effect(a, b, EffectKind::AddAbility(AbilityRef::delayed(card, 0)), Duration::AsLongAs(card, 0))` and the mirror, the `lasting[0]` condition being 'you control both'. `paired_with(q, id)` reads `q.state().effects.iter().find(|e| e.source == id && matches!(e.kind, EffectKind::AddAbility(_)))`. The soulbond trigger is `THIS_ENTERS` or `when(ZONE_CHANGE, another creature you control enters)`, offered only while both are unpaired.

object-reference-ring-bearer.note: No Ring-bearer in state or mechanics.

object-reference-scoped.how: Dream Halls: `spell_alternatives: &[SpellAlternative { applies: fn(q, asker, spell, player) .., cost: .. }]` has the spell in hand for `applies`. Demon of Fate's Design: `q.cost_objects(me)` for what was sacrificed. Soul Partition: `CostChange` keyed by the spell's exile grant.
object-reference-scoped.note: Low confidence; `unsure` for Dream Halls alone.
object-reference-scoped.partial: Dream Halls's cost is 'a card sharing a color with that spell': `InsteadOfManaCost` has to read the spell; not opened to the end. The 5 are distinct and only these 3 were looked at.

object-reference-sole-target-of.how: q.sole_target does not exist. Read state.targets(item) with left_stack as Leyline of Resonance does. 'Targets only a single' holds however many times it was chosen (115.9c), while OnStack(SingleTarget) counted them: both now told apart by the printed words.

object-state-controlled-since-before-com.note: controlled_since is by turn, not step.

object-state-cost-paid-madness.how: Grave Scrabbler: a trigger on Discarded with a cast by madness: read the Cast record's instead? Or an enters test on cast_from == Exile with history of own Discarded.
object-state-cost-paid-madness.partial: No flag read: inferred from cast_from and a discard this turn; not exact for a second cast.

object-state-cost-paid-prowl.how: way(cost, ZoneKind::Hand, text).condition(fn asking history for combat damage by subtype); 'if its prowl cost was paid': item.way == 1 for a spell; q.obj(id).cast_way == 1 for a permanent.

object-state-couldnt-attack.note: The declaration keeps no record of who could not attack.

object-state-devoured-a-creature.how: `e.chosen_number = Some(eaten.len() as u32)` in `enters`, read by `choose::chosen_number(q, asker)` in the static or ability.

object-state-embalmed.how: `q.obj(token).entered_with` or `Record.cause` on the token's creation names embalm's ability: `Cause::Ability { source, ability }`, then compare the ability's text. Embalm itself is an activated ability, and 'if this creature was embalmed' reads it from the copy's own `Copiable` exception, written in the same effect.

object-state-foretold.how: `q.history().all().iter().any(|r| matches!(r.event, Event::ZoneChange { object, .. } if object == c) && matches!(r.cause, ..foretell..))`, or `q.card(c).foretell.is_some()` on a face-down card in exile you own.
object-state-foretold.partial: A card with a granted foretell (Ranar, Alrund's Epiphany's cast) needs the special-action record; the plain read misses a card exiled face down otherwise.

object-state-had-to-attack.note: The declaration keeps no record of forced attackers.

object-state-non-basic-land-type.how: `chars.subtypes` holds land types: filter with `!matches!(s, Subtype::Plains | Subtype::Island | Subtype::Swamp | Subtype::Mountain | Subtype::Forest)` and a land type test.

The soulbond trigger is `THIS_ENTERS` or `when(ZONE_CHANGE, another creature you control enters)`, offered only while both are unpaired.
object-state-paired.note: Same machinery as row 12: one implementation answers all of rows 12, 13, 14 and 129.

object-state-renowned.how: As row 23: the `Done` note is the mark, ended by the new object id.

object-state-snow-mana-of-own-color-spen.how: Boreal Outrider: mana_spent_to_cast with a snow source and tally against the spell's colors, then a next_creature_counter style replacement.

object-state-started-turn-untapped.note: No `Untapped` event, and `TurnBegan` is not triggerable.

object-state-tribute-not-paid.how: Tribute: enters: Some(fn(g, entering)) asks g.ask for an opponent (choose::player), asks them yes/no (effects::ask_may), adds entering.counters[PlusOne] += N, and records the refusal; 'if tribute wasn't paid': an intervening if: when(THIS_ENTERS) with .condition reading Obj state. The refusal can be a data word (Obj.chosen) or the absence of a Counters Event: a shared mechanics/tribute.rs of 30 lines.
object-state-tribute-not-paid.partial: Checked only that an enters fn may ask (number_as_enters does). No keyword: reminder text only; a -1/-1-counter-based replacement of the counters still counts as paid, the rule says paid.

object-state-unearthed.how: `Event::Done` from unearth's ability, read by the object's id, or `q.obj(id).cast_way` for the way.
object-state-unearthed.partial: Malfegor Avatar is a Vanguard: blocked by card type whatever the read. Unearth is an activated ability, not a way, so `cast_way` does not apply.

objects-that-paid-a-cost-at-resolution.how: A discard paid next to mana lands, read from the Discarded records since the payment began, last first (Wolf of Devil's Breach). Blight lands through blight::may_in_effect (Grub). Fable of the Mirror-Breaker is a data bug: the source has DiscardNumberCards(2), but the Oracle text says 'up to two'. Held as 'discard of up to a number read as exactly that number'. Moonring Mirror and Duplicity are held: no ruling says whether exiling an empty hand counts as 'if you do'. A read of counters removed alone no longer claims this hole. Swift Warkite, Winter, Tunnel of Love and Triumph of Saint Katherine wait on other forms.
objects-that-paid-a-cost-at-resolution.partial: Two questions rather than one payment.

offering.note: Offering reduces by the sacrificed permanent's whole mana cost, colored symbols too. Emerge reduces by mana value only.
offering.partial: way(Cost{emerge: true, permanents: sacrifice, ..}, Hand).instant_speed() is a generic-only stand-in.

one-or-more-that-die-read-as-each-in-the.how: The data's trigger is WhenAPermanentDies(And([Other(ThisPermanent), And([IsCreatureType(Cat), ControlledByAPlayer(SinglePlayer(You))])])) where Oracle says 'Whenever one or more other Cats you control die' (Ajani; the Bee's and Townsfolk's are other creatures): a batch that triggers once (CR 603.2c), as WhenAnyNumberOfCreaturesOrPlaneswalkersDie(..) reads it. Read as each, two Cats dying together trigger twice.
one-or-more-that-die-read-as-each-in-the.note: Ajani, Nacatl Pariah; Great Fierce Bee; Vengeful Townsfolk.
one-or-more-that-die-read-as-each-in-the.partial: With the data right, the -4 still needs one permanent choosable for several types (cantrip_mechanics::each_opponent_keeps_one_of_each_type), and the trigger asks to exile Ajani when he is gone.

operation-any-player-may-pay.how: Icy Prison: loop over players in turn order, g.may_pay(p, ..); stop at a yes; else sacrifice.

operation-attach-chosen.how: Not landed: the one card holds on another hole.
operation-attach-chosen.partial: To a player (Archnemesis, Maddening Hex, The Unluckiest Planeswalker, 3 cards): attach takes ObjectId host, no form.

operation-attach-each.how: Attach to a player has no call (corrections of the last pass). Archnemesis, Ardenn, Maddening Hex.
operation-attach-each.partial: To a player (Archnemesis, Maddening Hex, The Unluckiest Planeswalker, 3 cards): attach takes ObjectId host, no form.

operation-bid.how: A loop in turn order over choose::number(g, player, source, least, most, ..) until all pass; the winner and amount are locals.
operation-bid.partial: No bid module; a player's life as the top limit is the card's to read.

operation-change-combat.partial: A printed AttackRule covers "only these" as a static.

operation-change-zone.how: Landed for one per card type, total mana value, same names and the like (Atraxa, Hurkyl, Portent of Calamity, Revival Experiment, Moorland Rescuer, Stroke of Luck, Karn Scion, Mangara's Tome, Parallel Thoughts). What is left: Cantrip's FaceDown is Manifested or Cloaked, so 'face down as a 2/2 stated creature' (Cybership, Death in Heaven, The Cyber-Controller, The Moonbase, Tezzeret Cruel Machinist) has no call; these hold as 'put onto the battlefield face down as a stated creature'. Technomancer is a data bug: the source reads ReturnAnyNumberOfGroupCardsMilledThisWayToBattlefield with no group rule of total mana value.
operation-change-zone.partial: One card per type: part with a matching: see target-constraint-one-for-each. A face-down exile pile as one thing (Mangara's Tome): linked exile list, no ordering guarantee.

play-permission-to-play-land.partial: For Shaman's Trance's spells, allow_play per card covers those there now.

play-permission-with-an-effect-on-what-i.how: The audit's how is wrong for most. Urianger needs a reduction PlayGrant lacks, Kaldring needs enters_tapped which is lands only (z.reason == PlayLand), Tomb of Aclazotz needs spell_replacement which only GrantedWay has. Each now names its own engine hole. Fires of Mount Doom, Apple and Ruinous are a delayed trigger reading the played card and stay as they were.

play-permission-with-mana-as-though-any-.how: PlayGrant/ExileCast any_type lets colored mana pay {C}, and all 23 cards print 'any color' over cards an opponent owns or a library holds, so any card with {C} in its cost plays wrong. It cannot be narrowed by a per-card test either: for such a card any_type: false is too narrow. Cantrip has no any-color field on a permission; spend_any_color is a battlefield rule that dies with its source. Only Robber of the Rich (hand-written) spells any color as any_type, and that is itself a deviation.
play-permission-with-mana-as-though-any-.partial: Any type is wider than any color only on {C} symbols: colored mana would pay {C}. Exact only with a permanent's spend_any_color rule, which needs it to stay on the battlefield.

play-permission-with-one-mana-as-though-.note: Abstruse Appropriation, Draugr Necromancer: PlayGrant cannot say which mana.

static-rule-assign-damage-to.partial: attacker_division offers no division with no blockers and no way to assign to a creature not in combat with it.

static-rule-attach-only-to.note: Partly writable: equip(..).targets(filter) handles the common case.
static-rule-attach-only-to.partial: A filter on the Equip ability covers Equip alone. Other attach effects and the 704.5n check go through host_allows, which reads no rule of the Equipment.

static-rule-attack-drags.partial: Attack requirements come from Chars::must_attack and effects, and are unconditional; none depends on who else is declared. attack_rules forbid one pair.

static-rule-attack-exception.how: Not landed. attacks_despite_defender and attack_rules both exist; the rule needs a read of the defender's last turn: Weathered Sentinels.
static-rule-attack-exception.note: The despite rule has no target argument, so the two tables work together.

static-rule-attack-exception-summoning-s.note: AttackRule only forbids; summoning sickness is checked in core.

static-rule-attacks-when-attacking.partial: As static-rule-attack-drags: a requirement conditional on the declaration has no form.

static-rule-block-capacity.note: blocks.rs rejects a second block with "can block only one creature" (509.1a). BlockRequirements has per-attacker limits and no per-blocker one. Verified after doubt; this one was the most likely misread and it is not one.

static-rule-block-while-tapped.note: blocks.rs candidates exclude tapped creatures; no rule list widens it.

static-rule-blocked-by-defender.how: block_rules testing attacker against what q.controller(blocker) controls: Graxiplon, Tanglewalker.

static-rule-blocks-despite.partial: can_block hard-codes flying, shadow and landwalk, then runs block_rules, which can only forbid. Giving the blocker Shadow would stop it blocking everything else, so no card-side form exists.

static-rule-blocks-only-if.how: Rule::BlocksOnlyIf does not exist; a block_rules function does it. Attacking player is the active player (506.2).

static-rule-cant-attack-defender-if.how: An attack rule function reading defending_player_of the attack, not the attacker's current defender, which has none as attacks are declared.
static-rule-cant-attack-defender-if.partial: The same cards' "can't block ..." halves are block_rules.

static-rule-cant-gain-ability.partial: No rule table for it, and a Layer::Ability removal runs in timestamp order, so a later grant wins. "Can't have or gain" needs a lock past timestamps.

static-rule-combat-cost-block.note: No block_costs: attack_costs is a fn to Option<ManaCost> read at declare attackers; BlockRule only says yes or no. Hollow Warrior taps a creature: also row 68. Archangel of Tithes, Awesome Presence, Cowed by Wisdom, Heat Wave, Hipparion, Myr Prototype, Oppressive Rays, Qal Sisma Behemoth, Whipgrass
static-rule-combat-cost-block.partial: The attack half of 'can't attack or block unless' is attack_costs.

static-rule-combat-damage-as-unblocked.note: turn.rs assignment reads Keyword/rule of the blocked attacker; nothing asks a rule list, and CardDef has no field for it.

static-rule-combat-group-attacker.partial: Per-creature AttackRule and per-target AttackLimitRule; blocked-by-count limits cover one attacker only.

static-rule-combat-group-blocked-attacke.partial: Per-creature AttackRule and per-target AttackLimitRule; blocked-by-count limits cover one attacker only.

static-rule-combat-group-blocker.partial: Per-creature AttackRule and per-target AttackLimitRule; blocked-by-count limits cover one attacker only.

static-rule-counter-limit.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: counter_bans: &[fn(q,asker,object,controller,kind)->bool]: true when object==asker.source, kind is dream and it has seven already.
static-rule-counter-limit.partial: The ban sees no amount, so a put of several is all or nothing; Rasputin puts one at a time.

static-rule-goaded-by.partial: chars.must_attack covers half of goad; "a player other than the goader" is read from EffectKind::Goaded only.

static-rule-may-exert.partial: Cantrip says so itself: a condition on AttackOption is not built; .condition would still offer and pay the exert.

static-rule-may-exert-with-nothing-linke.how: exert::as_it_attacks(no-op, 'You may exert...') for the offer, plus a triggered(when(EventMask::PAID_TO_ATTACK, fn)) on Event::PaidToAttack{option: AttackOption::Exert, ..} for 'whenever you exert a creature', as enlist does.
static-rule-may-exert-with-nothing-linke.partial: A no-op linked trigger shows on the stack. Exerts paid by a cost don't raise PaidToAttack: 'whenever you exert' misses Cost::exert. A silent AttackOption form would be cleaner.

static-rule-prohibit-activate.how: activation_rules is asked of a card in hand too: a creature card in hand is no creature, so a rule over the battlefield must test it is there, or Damping Matrix stops cycling.
static-rule-prohibit-activate.note: Forms overlap, so the row is 14 cards by 16 form memberships.

static-rule-prohibit-be-attached-by.partial: host_allows is closed: protection, then Equipment-creature or the Aura's enchant ability. Nothing on the host is asked. Protection from Auras would over-reach.

static-rule-prohibit-be-attacked.partial: Read for planeswalkers and battles only.

static-rule-prohibit-be-played.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: land_play_rules: &[fn].

static-rule-prohibit-counter-of-abilitie.note: The can't-be-countered keyword reaches spells only.

static-rule-prohibit-crew.how: activation_rules are asked of the Vehicle and CostPayment shows no tap, so a creature can't be barred from crewing.
static-rule-prohibit-crew.note: Forms overlap, so the row is 14 cards by 16 form memberships.

static-rule-prohibit-lose-counters.partial: counter_bans stops counters being put, not removed; remove_counters has no rule.

static-rule-prohibit-turn-face-up.how: activation_rules: &[fn] and crew is an activated ability; face_up_bans for turn-face-up.
static-rule-prohibit-turn-face-up.note: Forms overlap, so the row is 14 cards by 16 form memberships.

static-rule-require-combat-attack.how: chars.must_attack is an unaimed requirement. Must-attack-a-given-player has no static form: Galactus, Public Enemy.

static-rule-require-combat-be-blocked.note: block_requirements is exact only when a single creature of the kind can block.
static-rule-require-combat-be-blocked.partial: must_be_blocked(q,source,attacker) has no blocker kind and is satisfied by any blocker; block_requirements makes each able blocker required, too strict once two Eldrazi could block. "By two or more" (Gorm) has neither.

static-rule-require-combat-block.how: BlockRequirement is asked per attacker: a creature able to block two attackers is forced to double-block. The audit's 'counts differ only when two conflict' understated it.
static-rule-require-combat-block.note: Grand Melee, Invasion Plans, Iron Golem. Tracker says only effects can.
static-rule-require-combat-block.partial: One requirement per attacker rather than one for the creature; the counts differ only when two requirements conflict.

static-rule-tap-cost-uses-toughness.partial: The crew and saddle total reads c.power; damage_by_toughness governs combat damage only. Tapestry Warden's damage half is that table.

static-rule-tap-power-bonus.how: Audit named crew and saddle. Station reads the tapped creature's power with no keyword bonus: Stoic Star-Captain.
static-rule-tap-power-bonus.partial: Stoic Star-Captain's station half: station reads power in cantrip_mechanics::station with no bonus.

static-rule-targetable-despite.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: targeting_rules: &[TargetingRule{kind: TargetingRuleKind::IgnoreHexproof, applies: fn(q,source,object)->bool}].
static-rule-targetable-despite.partial: `applies` names no targeter, so "you control" is unread: exact with two players, too wide with three or more. Kaya's player half has no form: `applies` takes an object.

static-rule-unique.note: Nacatl War-Pride alone exists: blocker_limits Some(1) plus must_be_blocked.
static-rule-unique.partial: Eight unrelated rules. Zilortha, Ogre Enforcer: lethal damage is obj.damage>=toughness with no hook. Skullbriar, Me: counters do not survive a move. Tromokratis: no "unless all block" rule on the declaration. Panglacial Wurm: no cast window inside a search. Ghostly Flame: damage reads the source's r

static-rule-untap-step.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: untap_in_others_untap_steps: &[fn]: Horizon Boughs names all permanents.
static-rule-untap-step.note: Tests only; no hand-written card uses it yet.
static-rule-untap-step.partial: I Know All, I See All is a Scheme: blocked by the game mode, not this.

static-subjects-matching.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: StaticAffects is a plain function.

static-subjects-one.how: Not landed. Audit's StaticAffects is a plain function; q.chosen_object in the held code wasn't checked.

static-subjects-take.how: Not landed and not examined card by card this pass, so this verdict is unverified. Audit said: move_together.

stickers.note: Unfinity casual: no sticker sheet, no 'ticket counter', and no reason to add them outside a casual mode.

target-cardinality-exactly.how: Printed {X} (spell or activated): targets::X.between(0, TargetSpec::COUNTED) or .counted() for exactly X; Divide{total: TargetSpec::COUNTED} on a spell; of_x for "X plus 1". Triggered, count read from the game: .between(0,COUNTED).counted_by(fn(q,asker)->u32); event amount: .counted_by_amount(); reflexive: g.reflexive_trigger_counted(..). Source X and kicks are read automatically (trigger_counted). Spell or activated ability whose count is read from the game (Aether Burst, Reap, Bobbleheads, verse-counter cycle, Vile Requiem, Serra's Liturgy): no counted_by, but card code can: card-written Par
target-cardinality-exactly.note: Roughly 40 cards are the plain exists forms; about 25 need the together idiom; about 18 are the partial list. together is proven only for a rule, not yet as a count: no card uses it as a read count, so test first.
target-cardinality-exactly.partial: Spell/activated read-from-game via together: judged again at resolution (a changed count makes the whole slot illegal, guard it with a check that the item already has targets); players are not counted by together, so "any target" counts fail; not honoured with Divide. Still gap: X plus multikicker i

target-cardinality-per-player.how: Up to one for each player lands. A required one for each opponent (Blatant Thievery, Frenzied Gorespawn, Guff Rewrites History, Sylvan Primordial, Turf War, Vaevictis Asmadi) does not: TargetSpec::EACH_OPPONENT always has a minimum of 0, so there is no slot that requires one target for each opponent.
target-cardinality-per-player.partial: Inside a mode documented invalid; min 0 always; Chaos Mutation "different players" is a together rule.

two-costs-a-spell-kicks-with.how: Lands as kicker + OptionalCost::new, proved by scenario on Archangel of Wrath, Anavolver, Stronghold Arena, Hallar. Audit missed three things: (1) every generated reader of 'kicked' and 'times kicked' on another object has to ask kicked || (paid && def.kicker), or Hallar misses it; (2) two conditional 'enters with' replacements overwrite Entering::becomes, so a Volver kicked twice lost the first kicker's keyword, needing a merged EntersAs; (3) Illuminate cannot land: X in a mana cost beside a kicker is never announced (actions.rs: if let Some(k) = def.kicker takes the one number).
two-costs-a-spell-kicks-with.note: object.rs:52 names this case: 'a card with kicker and another optional cost is not ambiguous'. No hand-written card spells it this way yet.
two-costs-a-spell-kicks-with.partial: 'Whenever you cast a kicked spell' and 'if it was kicked' mean kicked only, so the second cost, being paid, doesn't read as kicked: OptionalCost{kicker: true} would set kicked but lose which. A card reads both fields; shared readers need item.kicked + item.paid.
